what: Detection-family pruning matrix: does the DSD 2026 protocol (400 incremental steps under GLOBAL ranking, >=10% of channels retained per prunable layer) transfer from CIFAR-100 classification to COCO detection?

protocol_under_test.quote: prune progressively over 400 incremental steps under global ranking, retaining at least 10% of the channels of every prunable layer
protocol_under_test.implementation_caveat: max_pruning_ratio is a PER-GROUP pre-step admission gate, not a per-layer clamp; the realized floor is 8.33%, not 10%. It also applies to in-channels. torch_pruning base_pruner.py:351-374, call site :464.

eval.note: ALL mAP below are POST-PRUNE / PRE-FINETUNE unless a row says otherwise; recovery fine-tuning is tracked separately in k1_recovery_summary.json

allocation_control_lite1.reading: global_pruning=True is NOT the dividing line: the same global allocator with random scores 0.0674 and with LAMP scores 0.1092, BEATING the local control (0.0820) while cutting its worst layer deeper (80.5% vs 91.7%). mAP is not monotone in min-survival. LAMP wins because it never touches stages 0-4.

allocation_control_lite2.note: lite2 was the rung the downstream robot deployed when this control was run; the deployment target moved to lite1 on 2026-08-22, so do not read 'lite2' as 'the deployed rung' anywhere below. allocation_control_lite2.reading: Structure transfers point for point. LAMP is relatively BETTER on lite2 than on lite1 at this operating point: 46.1% of baseline retained vs 33.9%. This pre-FT control was the only lite2 evidence when it was written; the full lite2 ladder finished 2026-08-26 and is in results/detection/full_scope_grid.json, where the post-recovery ordering agrees with lite1 rung for rung.

per_layer_floor_sweep_lite1.reading: NO. At every cap the five worst-hit layers are all in stages 1-2: the cap changes how DEEP the worst cut is, never WHERE it lands. cap=0.1 reaches a min survival (76.0%) comparable to LAMP's (80.5%) and is still 12x worse in mAP. Non-monotone in the cap itself (0.5 worse than 0.9). Consequence: the protocol sentence cannot be repaired by changing 10% to 50%.

The operator claim does not: only 83 of 479 operators ran on the TPU because of the onnx2tf EXPORT, not because of the graph. onnx2tf lowers the BiFPN fusion to a rank-5 CONCAT/SUM and timm's SAME-pool to PADV2, neither mappable, so the subgraph stopped at the backbone. The 83/396 vs 90/389 difference between the two 2026-06-19 compiles is not compiler nondeterminism either -- the tflite was re-converted between them (convert_20260619_151449.log; the compile logs record 4.45 vs 4.44 MiB for the same path). recovery_finetune_lite1.reading: Recovery fine-tuning compresses the pre-FT 273x gap to 1.48x. Two groups emerge: any allocation that leaves early-stage capacity intact (LAMP 94.0%, local-uniform 91.7% of baseline) versus the one that guts it (global+magnitude, 63.4%). Which healthy allocation you pick barely matters -- LAMP and local differ by 2.5% while the local arm actually cut MORE (9.17% vs 8.80% full-model). The pre-FT metric mispredicts both the magnitude AND the ordering: pre-FT LAMP led local by 33% (0.1092 vs 0.0820), post-FT that inverts to a 2.5% edge. Convergence differs: healthy arms flatten by ep5, the damaged arm still climbs at ep15, so 1.48x is an EQUAL-BUDGET gap, not a terminal one.
recovery_finetune_lite1.cross_budget_comparison: The cluster ran the same config (global+magnitude, full -9.0%) for 40 epochs on full train2017 and reached 0.2629. LAMP at 15 epochs on minitrain-25k reaches 0.3027: 4.7x less data, 2.7x fewer epochs, 15% higher mAP. Swapping the criterion beats scaling the training budget by an order of magnitude. Consistency check: this session's global+magnitude arm at the weaker budget gives 0.2043 < 0.2629, correct direction.

pareto_recovery_lite1.crossover_check: reid's measured table warned that global+LAMP can RELOCATE starvation and lose to local ranking at high ratios. That does NOT reproduce on detection: at full -44% LAMP scores 0.2555 vs local's 0.2201. The LAMP advantage WIDENS with depth (2.5% at full -9%, 16.1% at full -44%), so LAMP is the correct recommendation across the whole measured range, not just near the top.
pareto_recovery_lite1.reading: The recovered curve is far flatter than the pre-finetune numbers suggest: 8.8% -> 44.0% full-model reduction costs only 94.0% -> 79.3% of baseline mAP. The pre-FT metric diverges catastrophically with depth -- at full -44% it reads 0.0014 (0.4% of baseline) while the recovered model reaches 0.2555 (79.3%), a 180x discrepancy. Any Pareto or grid-truncation decision taken from pre-finetune numbers is wrong.

matched_pairs_vs_cluster.what: Head-to-head at near-identical full-model reduction: the cluster ran the published protocol (global ranking + magnitude_l2) for 40 epochs on full train2017 (118k); this session ran LAMP for 15 epochs on minitrain (25k).
matched_pairs_vs_cluster.reading: At matched reduction, swapping the criterion beats a 4.7x larger training set plus 2.7x more epochs -- and the margin WIDENS with depth (15% -> 20% -> 34%). Criterion choice matters more the harder you prune.

K5_narrowed_ignored_layers.question: Does narrowing ignored_layers to only the two output convs preserve accuracy, and does it actually free up capacity?
K5_narrowed_ignored_layers.answer: NO BENEFIT for the recommended criterion. Closed 2026-08-19 in ~10 GPU-minutes without needing a fine-tune, because the allocation itself settles it.

output_contract.free: their INPUT width (88, shared with the BiFPN) may shrink
output_contract.verified: out=810/36 held in every narrowed run

allocation_at_full_minus_44pct.note: IDENTICAL to the current ignore list -- LAMP never uses the freedom
heads do get cut, contract intact
cls_out fell to 709 -- confirms why the output convs must stay frozen

prunable_group_count.note: and the 4 that touch fpn reach BatchNorms and resample convs, not the BiFPN trunk

findings: With LAMP the narrowed and current ignore lists produce the SAME allocation, part for part. The extra freedom is never exercised, so narrowing is a no-op for the recommended criterion.
The BiFPN convolution trunk reads 0.0% cut under EVERY configuration tested, including one where nothing but the stem was ignored. It is not ignored_layers that protects it.
Narrowing IS mechanically safe for the output contract: out=810/36 held while the shared width fell 88 -> 72 and the head internals lost 23.5%/31.2%.

CAVEAT: the audit's claimed 98.29% ceiling from narrowing was NOT reproduced here. A deep-target run to check it timed out at 3000 iterative_steps and remains unverified. Since the BiFPN trunk never moves, that ceiling would have to come from head internals plus deeper backbone cuts, not from freeing the FPN.
K5_narrowed_ignored_layers.recommendation: Leave ignored_layers as it is. Narrowing adds risk and code churn for zero measured gain under the criterion we recommend.
